value.rationale: The finite two-colour rank-three representative problem is a recognized and difficult natural invariant. Complete classification of the first multiple-marker strata (k=2,3,4), including exact theory counts and sharp relative representative bounds, creates testable boundary data that is not reducible to the prior one-red table and gives a useful small-colour benchmark for finite-model type calculations. This is not an arbitrary random finite slice: fixing the number of minority-colour markers measures precisely the first interactions of distinguished positions. No claim is made about solving the unrestricted global optimum.
